lessons.title: Part 1: Constant of Proportionality & Unit Rates with Fractions
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Constant of Proportionality & Rates with Fractions
lessons.reading: Two quantities are in a proportional relationship when their ratio y/x is always constant. That constant k = y/x is called the constant of proportionality, giving the equation y = kx. When a rate involves fractions (like 3/4 mile in 1/2 hour), divide the first fraction by the second to find the unit rate.

principles.title: Constant of Proportionality (k = y/x)
principles.summary: Divide y by x to find the constant of proportionality k in y = kx.

principles.title: Unit Rates with Fractional Quantities
principles.summary: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions by dividing.

lessons.title: Part 2: Percent Change, Markup, Markdown & Tax
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Percent Problems, Tax & Discounts
lessons.reading: Percent change compares the amount of change to the original amount: Percent Change = (Change / Original) × 100%. For markups or sales tax, add the percent increase to 100%; for markdowns or discounts, subtract the percent decrease from 100%.

principles.title: Percent Increase, Decrease & Discounts
principles.summary: Calculate percent change, markups, and discounts from the original value.

lessons.title: Part 3: Simple Interest (I = Prt)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Simple Interest Formula I = Prt
lessons.reading: Simple interest is money earned on savings or paid on a loan. Use the Ohio Grade 7 formula I = P × r × t, where P is the principal (starting amount), r is the annual interest rate as a decimal, and t is the time in years.

principles.title: Simple Interest (I = Prt)
principles.summary: Multiply principal P by decimal rate r and time t in years.

lessons.title: Part 1: Adding, Subtracting, Multiplying & Dividing Integers
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Operations with Negative Numbers
lessons.reading: Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite: a − b = a + (−b). When multiplying or dividing two integers, same signs give a positive result and different signs give a negative result.

lessons.title: Part 2: Combining Like Terms, Distributive Property & Two-Step Equations
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Simplifying Expressions & Two-Step Equations
lessons.reading: Combine like terms by adding coefficients of the same variable. Use the distributive property a(bx + c) = abx + ac to clear parentheses. To solve a two-step equation like ax + b = c or a-x inequality, undo addition/subtraction first, then undo multiplication/division.

principles.title: Combining Like Terms
principles.summary: Add or subtract coefficients of like variable terms.

principles.title: Expanding with the Distributive Property
principles.summary: Multiply the outside factor across each term inside parentheses.

principles.title: Solving Two-Step Equations (ax + b = c)
principles.summary: Isolate the variable using inverse operations in two steps.

principles.title: Solving One- and Two-Step Inequalities
principles.summary: Solve linear inequalities and interpret solution sets.

lessons.title: Part 1: Scale Drawings, Circle Circumference & Area
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Scale Drawings, Circumference & Area of a Circle
lessons.reading: Multiply a drawing measurement by the scale factor to find the actual length. For any circle with radius r and diameter d = 2r, the circumference is C = 2πr (or πd) and the area is A = πr² (using π ≈ 3.14).

principles.summary: Use scale factors to convert between map measurements and real lengths.

principles.title: Circumference of a Circle (C = 2πr)
principles.summary: Calculate circle circumference using C = 2πr or πd.

principles.title: Area of a Circle (A = πr²)
principles.summary: Calculate circle area by squaring the radius and multiplying by π.

lessons.title: Part 2: Angle Relationships & Simple Probability
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Complementary/Supplementary Angles & Theoretical Probability
lessons.reading: Complementary angles add up to 90°, supplementary angles add up to 180°, and vertical angles are equal. The probability of a simple event is the number of favorable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes.

principles.title: Complementary, Supplementary & Vertical Angles

principles.title: Simple Theoretical Probability
principles.summary: Compute probability as favorable outcomes over total possible outcomes.
